summary: 17 load-bearing claims re-checked with 38 independent WebSearch queries (WebFetch/curl egress-blocked; no budget error hit). Verdicts: 12 confirmed, 5 corrected, 0 unverifiable, 0 refuted. Core Whoop facts hold (Series G $575M at $10.1B on 2026-03-31; $199/$239/$359 tiers; $49/$79 upgrade-fee reversal on 2025-05-10; FDA letter 2025-07-14; CBP N339661 HTS 9031.90.9195+9903.88.01). Corrections: (1) FDA close-out is now a primary fda.gov letter dated 2026-06-17 (not just 'reported 06-23'); (2) Helio Strap MSRP is $99.99 not $99; (3) Fitbit FY2018 GM was 39.9% GAAP/40.9% non-GAAP and '43%' for 2017 is the non-GAAP figure; (4) 2025 smart-ring volume/growth mixes analysts - IDC says ~4.3M units +49%, Counterpoint +77%; (5) the 'India rings are the bright spot' framing is wrong - IDC has Indian ring shipments down 30.6% in 2025 with ASP down 8.7% to $160, even though Ultrahuman's 30.4% share and INR 28,499 no-sub price are right. Biggest staleness: Oura's 2026-09-03 S-1 (9-mo revenue $1.21B +74%, 5.0M paid members, 55% GM, 89% membership GM, ~85% 12-month retention, S&M $103M) replaces every Oura number and is the only primary churn/CAC-proxy source found; Google's Fitbit Air ($99.99 screenless band, May 2026) is entirely missing and materially changes the price-floor argument; Whoop's Feb 2026 Passive MSK update makes strength load automatic (no logging) though rep/exercise identification is still absent; Amazfit Helio Strap Pro ($199.99, June 2026) and FORT ($349 retail + $80/yr, slipped to Q2 2027) show the segment moving toward movement intelligence. Gaps remain for wearable-specific return rates and any primary DTC CAC figure.
